text:
luca: FYI I reproed a cross-request KV contamination when a long-context request was split across batches and a prefetch landed in the wrong page. Seen on main with nightly load test.
maya: ugh. can you paste the minimal repro logs?
luca: here's the tail from the worker (redacted). note the request ids and the page swaplines.
```
[2026-03-17T22:12:03Z] req=0x7f1a2a gen_id=613 page=42 tag=0x11f2 append: slot 128 -> page#42@offset 8192
[2026-03-17T22:12:03Z] req=0x7f1a2a prefetch page#43 for seq 2048
[2026-03-17T22:12:03Z] req=0x8b2c3b gen_id=614 page=42 tag=0x11f3 read: page#42@offset 0 -> returned block.tag=0x11f2
[2026-03-17T22:12:03Z] WARNING kvcache: fingerprint mismatch, expected tag=0x11f3 got 0x11f2 (possible stale)
```
luca: note two different req handles pointing at same page id; later the decode pipeline used the wrong KV blocks and we saw token misalignment in output.
anya: Is this the batch-split logic that writes partial frames? Could be we reuse page slots before pointer update completes.
sam: maybe the slot recycling timer is too aggressive under high concurrency. Did you reproduce with prefetch disabled?
luca: yep — disabling prefetch makes the bug go away (no split-flight). repro script attached in gist- will paste after thread.
maya: sounds like race between prefetch completion and eviction; the prefetch attaches a temp ref then we evict and reassign page id -> stale tag observed.
perf-bot: perf/kvcache memory_growth test 2026-03-17 22:00 triggered +12% RSS on worker-7 during long-context run. Regression window: 2026-03-16 -> 2026-03-17
anya: Can someone check if request-scoped epoch tagging was regressed in last kernel-selection change? We recently removed the piggybacked req-epoch write to avoid a memcpy.
sam: I recall a change: "defer_epoch_write" patch landed in PR #4821. That deferred writing epoch until post-append to reduce memcpy overhead. Maybe it introduced a window where a page receives a fresh slot id but old epoch left behind.
maya: good call. luca, can you try reverting that locally and repro?
luca: reverted locally -> immediate pass, no stale tag warnings in logs. So likely the deferred-epoch write created a small window where page header had new page id but stale epoch/tag.
anya: mitigation idea: make page assignment atomic (write header with new tag and epoch together) or include request generation id into slot pointer so mismatch is impossible.
sam: short-term: disable defer_epoch_write and re-backfill the memcpy; longer-term: add an atomic header update + assert in debug builds that header.tag == fingerprint(header.epoch, page_content)
maya: also we should add a regression test that fuzzes batch-split + prefetch with heavy concurrency and checks kvcache fingerprint invariant after every page op.
perf-bot: created perf job: "kv-batch-split-fuzz" with 1000 iterations, concurrency 16. link: https://perf.redwood.internal/job/kv-batch-split-fuzz/219876
luca: I'll open a PR to revert the defer_epoch_write and add the debug assertion + test. tagging @anya @sam for review.
anya: assign to eng-runtime oncall for immediate patch + canary push. ops-bot: schedule canary to 3% traffic and monitor kvcache/fingerprint errors for 30m.
ops-bot: Canary scheduled: canary-id=c-219876, traffic=3%, window=30m. Notify: #eng-oncall #eng-runtime.
sam: also add an observability metric: kvcache.fingerprint_mismatch.count and kvcache.prefetch_racy.count so we can detect recurrence.
maya: nice. luca can you include the small repro script + exact worker binary sha in the PR so QE can run it?
luca: will do. binary sha: sha256:8a7f3b...; repro gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/kvcache-swapline-repro
anya: after revert + canary, let's plan root cause followup to make header updates atomic and consider ref counting semantics for prefetch to avoid early reuse.
maya: thanks everyone. tagging docs: devex, add KB entry under "kvcache hazards" for this class of race.
luca: thanks, will draft the PR now. :thumbsup:
